name: Digital Nomad Visa

requirements.blocker_text: Requires stable and sufficient net monthly income of at least EUR 3,500, from employment by a company registered outside Cyprus or self-employment serving overseas clients.
requirements.fix_path: Document qualifying monthly income before applying.

requirements.blocker_text: Must not work for a Cyprus-based employer or perform local economic activity.

evidence_required.document: Proof of remote employment/self-employment with non-Cyprus employer/clients
Proof of income at or above EUR 3,500/month
Entry as a visitor, then application to the Civil Registry and Migration Department within 3 months of arrival

outcome.duration_length: 1 year, renewable up to a total of 3 years

sources.title: KPMG Cyprus -- Cyprus Digital Nomad Visa Scheme (summarising the Council of Ministers decision)
VisaHQ news -- Cyprus Digital Nomad Visa Cap Raised to 1,000 (reporting a Deputy Ministry of Migration and International Protection announcement, Oct 2025)

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Cyprus's initial build. STATUS SET TO DRAFT: this scheme is a real, actively-administered Council of Ministers decision (confirmed by an official Deputy Ministry announcement per visahq's reporting), but gov.cy's own announcement page returned HTTP 403 to automated fetching in this pass -- the underlying figures are corroborated consistently across multiple independent tier-3/4 sources (KPMG's professional tax-alert summary and news coverage of the government's own October 2025 cap-raise announcement), which is reassuring but does not substitute for a directly-read tier-1 source. The annual cap (raised from 500 to 1,000 permits as of October 2025) is modelled via application_window.cap_type = 'fixed_number' rather than as a fake requirement; selection_method set to 'first_come' to reflect that permits are granted within that cap rather than merit-ranked, distinct from most other digital-nomad routes in this dataset which are uncapped ('assessed'). Does NOT lead to permanent residence or citizenship -- consistent with how most digital-nomad routes in this dataset are modelled.
